h: A Few Tricks for the Tropical Course
p: Want a fighting chance at the top of the leaderboard? Crazy golf rewards patience more than power. Look at each hole before you hit and spot the slopes, the walls you can bounce off and the obstacles you'll need to dodge. A gentle putt in the right direction almost always beats a hopeful whack, and you'll spend far less time chasing your ball back down the course.

Before you tee off, agree a couple of house rules with your group. A maximum of six shots per hole keeps things moving, and letting little ones take a second go on the tricky ones keeps the mood sunny. Write the scores down as you go, because arguments about who got what on hole seven are almost guaranteed otherwise.

There's plenty more to see in Derby when you're done. Derby Museum and Art Gallery is home to a fine collection of paintings by Joseph Wright of Derby, the city's famous 18th-century artist, and Pickford's House gives a glimpse of Georgian family life. If you'd rather be outdoors, Markeaton Park is a big, popular green space with play areas and room to roam, while Kedleston Hall, a grand National Trust house, is just outside the city. Mix and match and you've got a full day out with something for everyone.
